Convert a sampling geometry to a footprint SD

Source: R/joint_scales.R
footprint_sd.Rd

Experimental. Returns the per-axis standard deviation, in map units, of the area over which a response is measured. multiScale_joint() uses it to relate the apparent scale of effect in a data set to the ecological scale (scales = "footprint").

Usage

footprint_sd(
  type = c("point", "disk", "square", "rectangle", "halfnormal"),
  size = NULL,
  width = NULL
)

Arguments

type

Sampling geometry: "point" (no footprint), "disk" (counts or detections within a fixed radius), "square" (a square plot or grid cell), "rectangle" (a plot or transect strip), or "halfnormal" (animals detected with a half-normal detection function, as in distance sampling).

size

Radius for "disk", side length for "square", length for "rectangle", and the detection-function scale for "halfnormal", in map units. Ignored for "point".

width

Width for "rectangle", in map units.

Value

A numeric vector of footprint SDs in map units.

Details

The SD is the square root of the per-axis variance of a point drawn at random from the footprint, weighted by detection where that applies: r / 2 for a disk of radius r, L / sqrt(12) for a square of side L, sqrt((L^2 + W^2) / 24) for an L by W rectangle (its two axes averaged, since the Gaussian kernel is isotropic), and the detection scale itself for a half-normal detection function, whose detection weights over the plane form a bivariate normal distribution.

See also

multiScale_joint(). vignette("v16-joint-data-sets", package = "multiScaleR") uses a footprint for acoustic recorders.

Examples

footprint_sd("disk", 100)          # 100 m fixed-radius point count: 50
#> [1] 50
footprint_sd("halfnormal", 60)     # distance sampling, sigma = 60 m: 60
#> [1] 60
footprint_sd("rectangle", 200, 20) # 200 m by 20 m transect strip
#> [1] 41.02845
